newsitem.title: KENYA: Special board boosts turnover at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Special board boosts turnover at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Two deals traded on the three-day offer board boosted turnover at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Monday, bourse officials said.

The NSE's 20-share index lost 9.65 points to stand at 3102.40. Turnover was posted at 23.233 million shillings traded on 556,535 shares from 13.220 million shillings traded on 244,739 shares on Friday.
Some 218,454 shares of Kenya Breweries traded unchanged at 50 and 156,403 shares of Diamond Trust Bank Kenya at 32 unchanged were transacted on the Three-Days offer board.
Brokers and bourse officials said activity on other boards was low. On average prices on key shares eased.
Sasini Tea & Coffee traded at 59.50 from 60.50 while Kenya Airways eased to 8.40 from 8.60. Kenya Commercial Bank shed 2 to close at 70.
"In fact, active trading went on during the first hour only after which most people just sat down. Many traders are doing what we call window-dressing," a bourse official said.
"We don't expect much activity in the market. The Christmas mood is still on and most brokers do not want a lot of paperwork.
Some dealers said they expected activity to pick up after the New Year.
But some brokers said they could not say for certain that the market will improve in the next year.
"The scenario is pretty different this year. If you had asked me at the end of 1994 whether prices might improve, I would definitely have said yes," one broker said.
He said bonus issues that accompany year-end results announced sometime between December and February no longer excited investors as most prices in the market were already overpriced.
"The market is also saturated with investors. Maybe the new issues might boost the market," another trader said.
Serena Hotels, African Tours & Hotels and Mumias Sugar Company are expected to issue shares sometime next year.
Another broker said he expected selling pressure from investors wanting to offload their shares to meet financial obligations to keep prices at their current low levels.
There were no transactions on the Foreign investors board.
Bamburi Cement traded at 29.25 from 29.50 while Total Kenya eased to 65 from 66.
